Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Shakuntala sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.68.18–80 and 1.69.1–28 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid), told in the text's order: the king, though he remembered, said he did not (1.68.18–19: the hook); she stood as if senseless with grief, still as a post, her eyes copper-red with anger, her lips quivering, looking at him sidelong as if to burn him, holding in the fire her austerity had gathered (1.68.20–22: `stood`); she said: knowing, why do you speak like a common man; your heart knows the truth and the lie (1.68.24–25); you think "I am alone"; you do not know the ancient seer who dwells in the heart (1.68.27: `heart`); sun and moon, wind and fire, sky, earth, water, the heart, Yama, day and night, both twilights and Dharma know a man's conduct (1.68.29; not voiced, in the picture); a wife is half the man (1.68.40) and the son is the self born of the self (1.68.47: `wife`); look at my son as at a second self in a clear pool (1.68.64; in the picture of `wife`: the boy's reflection in the polished floor wears a crown); abandon me if you will, but not your own son (1.68.71); the king: I do not know a son born of you; women speak untruth; who will believe your word (1.68.72); your mother Menaka, pitiless, cast you off on the Himalaya like a used garland (1.68.73: `insult`, the turn); I do not know you; go as you please (1.68.80: the title); she: you see others' faults small as mustard seeds and not your own, large as bilva fruit (1.69.1; not voiced); truth weighed against a thousand horse sacrifices outweighs them (1.69.22: `truth`); there is no law higher than truth (1.69.24); even without you, Duhshanta, my son will rule this four-cornered earth (1.69.27: `leave`); having said so much she set out; then a bodiless voice from the sky spoke to Duhshanta among his priests and ministers (1.69.28: the cliffhanger). The speeches are short paraphrases of single verses, each cited on screen. He names her mother Menaka in the insult; we say "your own mother" (the names-per-10-s rule). CE AGAINST THE POPULAR STORY, said on screen in the source line and a tag: in the epic the king does not forget her; the ring and the curse are Kalidasa's.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

loop.hookQuestion: What does Shakuntala answer a king who denies her?
loop.prevQuestion: What will Shakuntala say to a king who denies her?
loop.openQuestion: Whose voice spoke from the sky, and what did it say?

strings.recapLine: Before his court a king said he did not know his wife or her son.
strings.sourceLine: Adi Parva 1.68–69 · no ring, no curse: those are Kalidasa's · BORI Critical Edition

lines.text: The king remembered her, and denied her.
lines.say: The king remembered her, [p:120] and denied her.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a statement; no fire): the king's hand, large in the foreground, gripping the throne's arm; the focus racks past it to a woman in bark cloth far down the dark hall, a child beside her. The card low and left.

lines.text: King Dushyanta sat enthroned. Before him stood Shakuntala, with their son.
lines.say: King Dushyanta sat enthroned. [p:250] Before him stood Shakuntala, [p:80] with their son.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): a crane down the red-and-gold hall from the high throne to the two small figures on the floor (plaques: Dushyanta · a king of Puru's line; Shakuntala · raised in a forest hermitage). A tag for three seconds: In the epic he never forgets her. The ring and the curse are Kalidasa's.

lines.text: She stood like a pillar: eyes red with anger, lips trembling.
lines.say: She stood like a pillar: [p:200] eyes red with anger, [p:120] lips trembling.
lines.note: STORY 1 · THE CLOSE-UP (wrath-crimson; answers episode 56's question: she does not plead): her face fills the frame: stunned, then the brows come down and the eyes burn; a sidelong look up at the throne; the mouth trembles and sets.

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "You think you are alone. The ancient witness sits in your own heart."
lines.say: You think you are alone. [p:300] The ancient witness [p:80] sits in your own heart.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (pure-flame; answers the hook): a tilt up from the king on his throne, small now, to the vault above him, where a ring of watchers stands in the dark blue: sun and moon, wind and fire, day and night; and in his own chest a small steady light (sub: Adi 1.68.27–29).

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "A wife is half of a man. A son is his own self, born again."
lines.say: A wife is half of a man. [p:350] A son [p:60] is his own self, [p:100] born again.
lines.note: STORY 3 · NEW LIGHT (island-gold: light from a high window falls on her and the boy): she stands straight, a hand on the boy's head; the boy, half hidden behind her at first, steps out into the light (sub: Adi 1.68.40, 47).

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "See yourself in him, as in clear water."
lines.say: See yourself in him, [p:200] as in clear water.
lines.note: STORY 4 (yamuna-deep): the hall's floor becomes still water: the boy stands at its edge looking down, and the face that looks back from the water wears a crown: the king's own face, younger (sub: Adi 1.68.64). A slow push.

lines.speaker: dushyanta
lines.text: "I know no son of yours. Women lie. Your own mother threw you away like a faded garland."
lines.say: I know no son of yours. [p:250] Women lie. [p:300] Your own mother [p:60] threw you away [p:60] like a faded garland.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE TURN (≈ 50 %) after a real silence (dice-vermilion): seen from the floor, a tilt up the throne steps to the king on his feet, an arm flung out; a withered garland drops down the steps into the foreground (sub: Adi 1.68.72–73). The word of the turn: DENIED.

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "Weigh a thousand horse-sacrifices against truth: truth is heavier."
lines.say: Weigh a thousand horse-sacrifices [p:80] against truth: [p:300] truth is heavier.
lines.note: STORY 6 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT · NEW LIGHT (seat-ivory): a great pair of scales fills the frame: in one pan a herd of small white horses and altar fires, piled high; in the other a single small flame; the flame's pan sinks slowly to the ground (sub: Adi 1.69.22). A slow orbit.

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "Even without you, my son will rule this earth."
lines.say: Even without you, [p:250] my son will rule this earth.
lines.note: STORY 7 (a second real silence before it): she takes the boy's hand and turns her back on the throne; a pull back down the hall as she walks toward us, courtiers parting (sub: Adi 1.69.27).

lines.text: She turned to go. Then a voice spoke from the sky.
lines.say: She turned to go. [p:400] Then a voice [p:80] spoke from the sky.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger; CE 1.69.28): she at the great doors, a hand on the boy's shoulder; a tilt up: the hall's roof is gone into bright sky, and every head in the court is lifting toward it. The source line (top).

lines.text: Next: The Voice from the Sky
lines.note: The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
